examples.solution_text:
Acceleration is the gradient: change in speed divided by the time taken for that stage.

From $0$ to $4$ s:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Acceleration}&=\frac{16-0}{4-0}\\&=4\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$

From $4$ to $10$ s:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Acceleration}&=\frac{16-16}{10-4}\\&=0\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$
The graph is horizontal: the car travels at a constant speed of $16$ m/s.

From $10$ to $14$ s:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Acceleration}&=\frac{0-16}{14-10}\\&=-4\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$
The deceleration magnitude is $4$ m/s².

From $14$ to $18$ s, the speed stays at $0$, so the car is stationary and its acceleration is $0$ m/s².

From $18$ to $24$ s:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Acceleration}&=\frac{12-0}{24-18}\\&=2\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$
Use the $6$ seconds after departure; exclude the time spent stationary.

Vehicle A:

$\begin{aligned}\text{Initial acceleration}&=\frac{24-0}{4-0}\\&=6\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Final deceleration magnitude}&=\frac{24-0}{16-12}\\&=6\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$

Vehicle B:

$\begin{aligned}\text{Initial acceleration}&=\frac{12-0}{6-0}\\&=2\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Final deceleration magnitude}&=\frac{12-0}{14-12}\\&=6\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$

Vehicle A accelerates faster. Both vehicles have the same deceleration magnitude: $6$ m/s².

coverage.summary: Removed the unsupported title key from all three candidate examples. All other candidate fields, example mathematics, diagrams and mappings are preserved. The baseline contains no existing worked examples. Practice and quiz mathematics were neither altered nor re-audited. Rendered typography and layout verification remain for the capture stage.

examples.derivation: The plotted endpoints give accelerations (16−0)/(4−0)=4, (16−16)/(10−4)=0, (0−16)/(14−10)=−4, (0−0)/(18−14)=0 and (12−0)/(24−18)=2 m/s². The car is stationary from 14 to 18 s. Departure lasts 6 s. These reuse the source's gradient, horizontal-segment and stage-selection methods.

From (2,3) to (8,12), acceleration is (12−3)/(8−2)=9/6=1.5 m/s². From (8,12) to (12,4), acceleration is (4−12)/(12−8)=−8/4=−2 m/s², giving deceleration magnitude 2 m/s². Solution steps correctly mark durations 6 and 4 s and speed-change magnitudes 9 and 8 m/s.

Vehicle A initially accelerates at 24/4=6 m/s² and finally decelerates at 24/(16−12)=6 m/s². Vehicle B initially accelerates at 12/6=2 m/s² and finally decelerates at 12/(14−12)=6 m/s². A accelerates faster; their deceleration magnitudes are equal. Colours, line styles and labels identify the vehicles consistently.
